slides.title: Who *owns* the network?
slides.body:
Not who runs it.
Who decides.

slides.title: Running it is easy
slides.body:
A team. A rota.
An escalation path.
A name in *seconds*.

slides.title: Deciding is harder
slides.body:
Who approves a standard
that constrains what a
business unit can *buy*?

slides.title: Or this
slides.body:
Who says the refresh
happens *this* year,
not next?

slides.title: Or this
slides.body:
Who settles it when security
wants segmentation and ops
wants a *shorter* window?

slides.title: What we find
slides.body:
Owned operationally by a team
with *no budget authority*.

slides.title: And
slides.body:
Owned financially by somebody
never asked a *technical*
question about it.

slides.title: So
steps: The standard is drafted, never ratified.
The refresh slips a year at a time.
The project has three sponsors and *no owner*.

slides.title:
It doesn't stop working.
It stops *changing*.
slides.body:
Which looks the same
for a while.
